Two friends and I went camping on a small island off the coast that you can walk to at low tide. We took mushrooms in the afternoon, around 2.5g each, and spent hours exploring rock pools. It was beautiful, the anemones were glowing and the sea sounded like breathing.

At some point I wandered off on my own to a rocky outcrop at the far end of the island to watch the sunset. I lost track of time completely. When I looked down, the water had come in all around the rock I was sitting on. The path back was under water. In my state, the sea looked like it was rising by the second, swallowing everything. I was sure that the whole island would disappear and that I'd drown. I screamed for my friends, but the wind took my voice.

It got dark. The water was black and loud, smashing against the rocks below me. I clung to the rock with both hands. My fingers were bleeding from the barnacles. I started seeing shapes in the waves, faces, arms reaching up. I was certain they wanted to pull me in. I felt my sense of self dissolving into the roar, like I was already part of the sea.

My friends had realised I was missing and were searching with their phone torches. They found me about two hours later. The tide had started going out again by then, and they waded out to me, knee-deep. I couldn't let go of the rock at first. They had to peel my fingers off one by one. Back at the tent I shook all night, wrapped in every sleeping bag we had. I kept hearing the waves as if they were inside the tent.

Ich war in einem Club und habe auf LSD die Toilette gesucht. In der Kabine ist das Schloss hängen geblieben, und ich bekam die Tür nicht mehr auf. Der Raum war winzig, das Licht hat geflackert und die Musik hat durch die Wände gedröhnt. Innerhalb von Sekunden war ich in Panik. Die Wände kamen näher, ich bekam keine Luft mehr. Ich habe gegen die Tür gehämmert und geschrien, aber niemand hat mich gehört. Ich war mir sicher, dass ich da drin ersticke und dass mich niemand findet, bis der Club schließt.

Irgendwann bin ich auf den Boden gesackt und habe mich nur noch zusammengerollt. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass die Kabine ein Sarg ist, in dem ich lebendig begraben bin. Ich weiß nicht, wie lange ich dort war, vielleicht zwanzig Minuten, vielleicht eine Stunde. Ein Türsteher hat schließlich die Tür von außen aufgebrochen, weil jemand gehört hatte, wie ich weine. Er hat mich nach draußen gebracht und mir Wasser gegeben, aber ich konnte die restliche Nacht nicht aufhören zu zittern.

I'm a trans woman. At the time of this experience, I had been living as myself for about three years and had started hormones two years before. I'd been struggling with anxiety and old family trauma, and I'd heard good things about ayahuasca from a friend. I found a retreat online that described itself as 'inclusive and heart-centred'. On the application form I wrote that I was trans. Nobody said anything about it.

When I arrived, the shaman, an older man from another country, seemed friendly. The facilitators were a European couple who translated for him. On the first evening there was a group circle where we introduced ourselves. When it was my turn, I said my name and that I'm a trans woman. The shaman said something to the facilitators, and they hesitated before translating. Eventually the woman said that the shaman 'honoured my journey' and that the medicine would 'help me find balance in my energies'. I felt a little uneasy but let it go.

The first ceremony was fine, mostly physical, a lot of purging. In the second ceremony, the shaman came to sit in front of me to do a 'healing'. He blew tobacco smoke over me and sang. Then he started speaking, and the male facilitator translated in a low voice. He said that he saw a 'masculine spirit trapped and suffering' inside me, and that he would help free it. He said the 'confusion' I was in was caused by a dark energy that had entered me in childhood. He pressed his hand hard on my chest, where my breasts are, and said he was 'removing the false feminine'.

I was deep in the medicine. I couldn't speak. I couldn't move. I wanted to scream at him to stop, but it was like my body belonged to someone else. And worse, part of me, in that state, started to believe him. I saw images of myself as a boy, the boy I was forced to be for so long, crying in a dark room. I saw my father's face, telling me to 'man up'. I felt that everything I had built, my name, my body, my life, was a lie and that I was being punished for it. I felt my identity crumbling, and I didn't know who I was anymore. Not a woman, not a man, just a shattered thing on the floor.

He went on singing for what felt like hours. At one point he called me by my old name, the name I haven't used in years, which I had never told anyone at the retreat. I still don't know how he knew it, maybe it was in my passport, which they had copied for registration. Hearing it in that state was like being thrown back into my childhood bedroom.

When the ceremony ended, I crawled to my bed and lay there shaking until morning. At breakfast the female facilitator came to me and said that she understood it was a 'challenging' night, but that the shaman was 'very powerful' and saw things we couldn't. She said that some people come to the medicine with 'mental constructs' that need to be released. I told her I wanted to leave. She said that leaving in the middle of the process could be dangerous for my spirit. I left anyway, that afternoon, with a taxi to the nearest town and a bus to the airport.

On the bus I kept touching my chest where his hand had been and feeling sick.
DMT at a party. I met an entity that looked like a clown made of light, and it laughed at me in a way that felt evil and mocking, like it knew I was a joke. It still creeps me out.

Ich war auf einem Psilocybin-Retreat mit einer Gruppe. Nach der Zeremonie sollten alle im Kreis erzählen, was sie erlebt haben. Ich fühlte mich gedrängt, sehr intime Dinge über meine Sexualität zu teilen, die während der Erfahrung hochgekommen waren. Ich war noch nicht ganz klar und habe Dinge gesagt, die ich niemals in einer Gruppe erzählen wollte. Danach habe ich mich nackt und bloßgestellt gefühlt. Einige Teilnehmer haben mich danach anders angeschaut, so kam es mir vor.

I'm a nervous flyer, and before a long-haul flight to visit family in Australia, a friend suggested I take a small dose of mushrooms to 'relax'. It was the worst advice I've ever received. I ate them in the airport toilet before boarding.

About an hour after take-off, the plane started to feel like a metal tube full of strangers breathing my air. The engine noise became a scream. Every bump of turbulence was the plane falling apart. I was certain we were going to crash and that everyone would die because of me, because I was carrying something evil onto the plane. I gripped the armrests until my hands cramped. The woman next to me asked if I was okay and I couldn't answer. Her face kept turning into a skull.

I went to the toilet and stayed there for a long time, until a flight attendant knocked and asked me to return to my seat because of turbulence. She noticed I was shaking and sweating and asked if I needed medical help. I said I was just a nervous flyer. She brought me water and checked on me every half hour, which was kind, but every time she came I thought she was about to say we were going down.

The effects faded after about five hours, but there were still nine hours to go. I spent them rigid in my seat, completely drained and terrified that it would come back. I didn't sleep. When we landed, I cried.
Ketamin auf einer Party, viel zu viel. Ich war im K-Loch und hatte das Gefühl, tot zu sein und nie mehr zurückzukommen.

I was taking an SSRI for depression and hadn't told the retreat about it, because I was afraid they wouldn't let me participate. I'd stopped it two days before, thinking that would be enough. It wasn't. About an hour after drinking ayahuasca, I started sweating heavily, my muscles were twitching, my jaw was clenching, and my temperature went up. My heart was pounding. I became extremely agitated and confused. The visions were chaotic and frightening, like being inside a malfunctioning machine. I knew something was wrong with my body. The facilitator realised it might be serotonin syndrome and they drove me to a hospital, where I was treated with cooling and medication. I was in intensive care overnight. I could have died.

My partner and I had been together for six years. We decided to take mushrooms together on a weekend away to celebrate our anniversary. It was meant to be romantic. About two hours in, we were lying in the grass by a river, holding hands, and he started crying. I thought it was a happy cry. Then he said there was something he had to tell me, that the mushrooms were showing him he couldn't hide it anymore. He told me he had been seeing someone else for eight months.

I don't think there's a worse place to hear that than at the peak of a mushroom trip. The world split in two. The river turned grey and the trees turned their backs on me. I felt like my entire life with him had been a film that had suddenly been revealed as fake, and that the 'real' world was cold and empty. I looked at his face and it kept changing, sometimes the man I loved, sometimes a stranger, sometimes something reptilian and cold.

I couldn't get away, we were in the middle of nowhere and neither of us could drive. I walked along the river for hours, crying and screaming at the sky. I felt like I was disintegrating. He followed me at a distance, crying too. I hated him for following me, and I was also terrified to be alone.

When the drug wore off we sat in the cottage in silence until morning. Then he drove us home and I moved out the next week.

Ich habe auf einer Party LSD genommen und bin beim Tanzen so unglücklich gefallen, dass ich mir den Fuß gebrochen habe. Ich habe den Schmerz kaum gespürt, aber mein Fuß sah völlig verdreht aus, und ich hatte panische Angst. Im Krankenhaus war alles grell und laut, und ich konnte den Ärzten kaum folgen.

I'm a firefighter. I'd been doing the job for 15 years and had seen a lot. A friend offered me LSD at a barbecue and I thought, why not, I'd done it in my twenties. Around the peak, someone threw some fat on the grill and it flared up. That was all it took. I was back in a house fire from three years earlier, where we didn't get to a child in time. I could smell the smoke, feel the heat on my face through the mask, hear the crackling. I saw the little body. I ran away from the barbecue and hid in the garden shed, shaking and crying. The fire kept burning in my head for hours. Everywhere I looked I saw flames, on the walls of the shed, on my own hands. I don't really remember the rest of the evening. My wife came to get me.

Ich hatte im Studentenwohnheim allein Pilze genommen und war in einer sehr düsteren Stimmung. Ich habe laut geweint und geschrien, weil ich das Gefühl hatte, dass mein Leben sinnlos ist. Meine Mitbewohnerin hat das gehört und gedacht, ich will mir etwas antun. Sie hat einen Krankenwagen gerufen, und mit dem Krankenwagen kam die Polizei. Ich war mitten im Trip, als plötzlich fremde Menschen in Uniform in meinem Zimmer standen und mich gefragt haben, ob ich mich umbringen will. Ich konnte nicht erklären, was los war. Ich habe nur geweint. Sie haben mich mitgenommen, in die Psychiatrie, und ich musste die Nacht dort verbringen. Das Zimmer war kahl, mit einem Fenster aus Milchglas und einer Tür ohne Klinke. Ich hatte das Gefühl, für immer eingesperrt zu sein. Am nächsten Morgen hat eine Ärztin mit mir gesprochen und mich entlassen, nachdem sie verstanden hatte, dass es die Pilze waren.
